claim: Kitcher/Strevens-style models show the community optimum is a mix of approaches, not everyone on the most promising one; credit-seeking (priority rule) can approximate that mix. Theoretical result; success functions are idealised.
agent_test: Compare all attempts on the top-ranked direction vs a code-set quota of attempts on untried directions, equal tokens, on open tasks with a grader.

claim: The Kitcher-type result is not robust to idealisation: when agents only see nearby agents, the majority sits on the easier project and none on the harder one (radius under 7); noisy beliefs about easiness shift the split toward the easier project. Own toy simulation (d21): credit-seeking allocation falls below a plain equal split once log-noise in success estimates is about 0.25 to 0.5.
agent_test: Test whether noisy difficulty estimates inside the agent make the allocation collapse onto the easy direction; add a code-held floor quota and compare. A toy simulation already predicts the floor quota wins at noise sd >= 0.5.

claim: In the Weisberg-Muldoon epistemic landscape, maverick (novelty-seeking) agents explore far more than followers or controls (400 mavericks 0.90 progress vs 400 followers 0.17); a few mavericks added to followers help more than proportionally. Thoma (2015) confirms the baseline numbers but shows the ranking depends on movement range.
agent_test: Mix of explorer and extractor attempts vs all-extractor at equal tokens; vary how far an attempt may jump from prior attempts.

claim: Mixed explorer/extractor groups beat pure groups at medium movement range (p<0.0001) and have far lower variance (SD 3.1 vs 12.5 points at step 150), but with strictly local movement a pure explorer group is ahead early (15% vs 8% at round 50) and the mix wins only by a tiny margin by round 300.
agent_test: Measure variance across seeds of the allocation rule, not only the mean; report SD with and without an exploration share.

claim: Cognitive diversity can beat individual ability in problem-solving groups (random agents 94.53 vs best agents 92.56 with 10 agents, l=12), but this is one simulation family on a random-value landscape, and Grim et al. 2019 show the result is sensitive to landscape randomness (abstract only; full text not opened).
agent_test: Do not use for single-answer voting (G4). For open-ended search, compare diverse-heuristic attempts vs top-scoring-heuristic attempts at equal tokens.

claim: Network connectivity effect is task dependent: partial connectivity raised cultural accumulation in humans (both level-3 innovations: 58.3% vs 0%, 12 groups per arm), while efficient networks helped on a single-peak landscape (peak found in 138/232 networked sessions; score 68 vs 39 independent when found).
agent_test: Vary how much attempts see of each other (none, scores only, scores plus methods) on a single-peak task and a combination-heavy task; compare.

claim: LLM agents that see only each other's scores follow the leader and converge on one approach: last-third HHI 1.00 vs 0.66, 1.00 vs 0.36, 0.82 vs 0.29 (baseline vs direction board); two-armed delegation shows insufficient exploration; independent agents concentrate on few targets.
agent_test: Log the share of attempts per direction (HHI) over a run; check whether the last third collapses; compare with a code quota.

claim: Putting the allocation in code removes in-context exploration failure: Qwen-7B inferior-peer lock-in 50.0% prompt-only, 23.3% with UCB formula in the prompt, 0.0% with a UCB calculator tool, 0.0% algorithmic UCB; GPT-4 shows suffix failure (best arm never chosen again) in over 60% of basic-prompt replicates.
agent_test: Replace model-chosen 'which direction next' with a code bandit rule; compare regret and lock-in at equal tokens.

claim: An explicit direction board plus claim check (max 2 agents per direction, one new direction per agent in round 1, pivot after 5 fruitless evals) gave 6 wins, 1 tie, 2 losses over 9 tasks vs the reproduced baseline (best of 3 runs), and opened 68 directions vs 41. Against the published MIT CORAL numbers it is 4 wins, 2 ties, 3 losses, losses to results obtained with web access and grader reading.
agent_test: Ablate the direction board, the cap of 2, and the pivot threshold (5) separately at equal tokens; no ablation exists in the source.

claim: Shared notes and skills across agents beat independent runs on some tasks (Kernel 1103 vs 1180 best of 4 independent; Polyominoes 84.2 vs 80.8), and removing sharing regresses (Kernel 1350 to 1601), but a plain 4-agent baseline beat a single agent on only 3 of 9 tasks.
agent_test: Compare N independent attempts, N attempts sharing notes, and N attempts with a direction board, equal tokens, 3 tasks.

claim: After a direction yields a record the system concentrates effort on it (76% of the remaining 38 evals); good allocation is explore early, exploit the champion later, not permanent spreading.
agent_test: Track exploit share after first pass; test a rule that shifts budget to the leading direction after first success.

claim: Diversity of approach or model raises accuracy in reasoning benchmarks: DIV-SE (GPT-4 Blocksworld 3: 94% vs SC-10 73%, graph colouring 97% vs 23%), three-model mix 91% vs same-model triple 82% on GSM8K, MoA multiple-proposer 61.3 vs single 56.7, SYMPHONY unique branches over 80% vs under 20%. Part of the gain may be extra sampling or model strength, not diversity alone. Counter: Self-MoA (one best model, many samples) beats a mix of models by 6.6 points on AlpacaEval 2.0 and 3.8 on average; in a regression of 70 mixtures per dataset quality outweighs diversity (alpha 2.6 to 4.7 vs beta 1.4 to 2.8).
agent_test: Strategy-diverse attempts vs same-prompt attempts at equal tokens on tasks with a check; keep selection by code (G5).

claim: Coverage rises steeply with repeated sampling (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples; MATH Llama-3-8B 82.9% to 98.44% at 10,000), but majority vote or reward model selection gains only 40.50% to 41.41%; finding and picking are separate problems.
agent_test: Report coverage and selected accuracy separately for each allocation rule.

claim: Same-model samples are homogeneous: only about 5% of 4000 generated ideas were non-duplicates (cosine >0.8); within-prompt similarity across 42 to 70+ models averages 0.82; most models give under 3 distinct answers in 10 queries.
agent_test: Count distinct directions among N attempts from one model with and without code-supplied seeds; that is the baseline for the allocation rule.

claim: Decoding or prompt tricks only partly restore diversity: verbalized sampling raises creative diversity 1.6x to 2.1x and recovers 66.8% of base-model diversity; in-context regeneration raises NoveltyBench diversity but does not reach humans; min-p still leaves 61.2% of pairs above 0.8 similarity.
agent_test: Compare verbalized-sampling prompts, temperature, and code-assigned directions on distinct-direction count at equal tokens.

claim: Evolutionary program-search systems report that novelty rejection, weighted parent sampling and bandit model ensembles each help over simpler alternatives (ablations; qualitative in our records).
agent_test: Add a code novelty filter (reject near-duplicate directions) and test on one open task; numbers needed from sources.

claim: Multi-agent LLM systems carry heavy overhead failures: failure rates 41% to 86.7% across 7 frameworks, with 36.9% inter-agent misalignment; division of labour has a cost that must be paid for.
agent_test: Count coordination failures in the scaffold's own logs; require equal-token win over single agent.

claim: More test-time compute on hypothesis generation improves quality in a tournament setting (Co-Scientist: Elo of top hypotheses rises across 10 time buckets over 203 goals), but the selector is a model-run tournament, which G8 distrusts.
agent_test: Do not adopt model-Elo selection; test only the spending side with a code check.

claim: The pivot threshold of 5 non-improving evaluations is shared by two systems, but neither source gives evidence that 5 is better than other values. In an own toy simulation (d23) the best threshold was 2 and 5 was never clearly best; with AIDE operators exploration settings made no difference in AIRA-dojo (d03).
agent_test: Sweep threshold 1,2,3,5,8 at equal tokens on one open task, with 10+ seeds (AIRA-dojo shows 3 seeds can flip rankings).

claim: Allocation rules that keep non-leader branches alive beat follow-the-best in LLM-agent search: DGM parent sampling 50.0% vs always-best-parent 39.7% (SWE-bench) and 38.0% vs 30.0% (Polyglot) vs no archive 23.0% / 14.0%; ShinkaEvolve weighted parent sampling beats hill climbing, which plateaus.
agent_test: Compare follow-the-best against a rule with a crowding penalty weight = score / (1 + attempts in direction) at equal tokens. Same-iteration comparison only so far, not same-token.

claim: Better exploration settings alone do not help when the attempt-generating prompt is weak: with AIDE's operators, MCTS, evolutionary search and UCT constants 0, 0.25, 0.75 all stayed near greedy on MLE-bench Lite; with improved operators every policy beat greedy (AIRA greedy 45.5 vs 39.8; MCTS 47.0).
agent_test: Check that the direction-proposal step forces genuinely different attempts before tuning thresholds or caps.

claim: A running memory of a single agent's own earlier attempts did not change results (AIDE with vs without memory, nearly identical medal rate); the authors scoped memory to sibling attempts to limit mode collapse, untested alone. Sharing only scores causes follow-the-leader (K07).
agent_test: Give the agent only the list of directions already tried and their outcomes, not a ranked leader board; compare with no notes at equal tokens.

claim: An agent's own score is a poor guide for allocation: in AIRA-dojo perceived (validation) medal rate keeps rising while held-out rate plateaus; picking the final node closes over 60% of the gap, and 3 top-k submissions add about 10%.
agent_test: Rank directions with code-computed scores; keep top 3 candidates to the end.

claim: Diversity predicts score but with less weight than quality: Self-MoA regression alpha(quality) 2.558/4.548/4.719 vs beta(diversity) 1.841/1.421/2.839 on MMLU/CRUX/MATH (R2 0.69 to 0.77); verbalized-sampling data raised downstream math accuracy from 30.6 (direct) to 36.1 (VS-Standard) and 37.5 (VS-CoT).
agent_test: Proposal prompt that asks for a list with probabilities, then a code duplicate filter (embedding similarity 0.95, as in ShinkaEvolve); score final result, not diversity.

claim: Known model-robustness problems: the Zollman less-connected-is-better result is not robust to parameters (Rosenstock et al. 2017); Weisberg-Muldoon's all-mavericks result is contested (Alexander et al. 2015, Thoma 2015). Only abstracts and a review were opened, no numbers.
agent_test: Do not hide earlier attempts from the agent on the strength of Zollman. Treat maverick dominance as model-dependent.

claim: Own toy models (not literature): code-set spread holds 83 to 91% of the optimum at any noise in success estimates, while credit-seeking by noisy self-estimates falls below it at about 30% to 65% error; in a sequential single-agent model a cap of 2 then exploit beat free attempts when the agent's own ranking is weak (rho 0 to 0.3) and lost when strong (rho 0.6); best pivot threshold 2, best explore share about 70% of the budget, both sensitive to how fast directions improve.
agent_test: Real run: free vs quota vs cap 2 vs graded crowding at equal tokens, pivot 1,2,3,5,8, explore share 0.33,0.5,0.7, on one open task with 10+ seeds. Measure the model's own direction-ranking correlation (rho) first.

claim: Coordination cost of simulated division of labour: in MAST failures split 41.8% design, 36.9% inter-agent misalignment, 21.3% verification; MAD does not reliably beat single agent plus self-consistency (e.g. GPQA single 0.33 vs Society of Mind 0.27; MMLU self-consistency 0.78 vs 0.76 single). A sequential one-agent scaffold removes the message-passing category but not design or verification failures. No single-agent baseline in MAST, so the overhead is not measured.
agent_test: Log spec-violation and verification failures of the scaffold itself; add a verify step after each allocated attempt (+15.6% task success in the one MAST intervention).

claim: Human field evidence on spreading: 30 years of MEDLINE (Rzhetsky et al. 2015) show scientists choose conservative problems and become more so; the inferred strategy is over 3x more costly than the best alternative for the bulk of the network and the best 50% strategy is nearly 10x more efficient than random. No counts of researchers per approach (peptic ulcer, funding portfolios) were found.
agent_test: Treat crowd drift to the safe direction as the default for any unforced allocation.
